people: Cao Si Kiem (Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam, 1989-1997; DongA Bank independent board member from March 2012; Chairman of DongA Bank's management board from 26 April 2014 to 2015)
summary: Vietnam News reports that DongA Bank's annual general shareholders' meeting on 26 April 2014 elected Cao Si Kiem as chairman of its management board, and that Kiem was Governor of the State Bank of Vietnam from 1989 to 1997. The same report notes this was the first time a former State Bank governor had taken the top job at a commercial bank. VietnamNet adds that Kiem had joined DongA Bank's board as an independent member in March 2012 and resigned the chairmanship in 2015, citing health reasons, and was replaced by Vo Minh Tuan. Both sources describe DongA Bank only as a joint-stock commercial bank; neither says in words whether it is privately or state-owned, so that point is unconfirmed by the sources used here.
source_title: DongA Bank appoints Kiem as chairman (Viet Nam News / bizhub)
move: central bank governor to chairman of DongA Bank, a joint-stock commercial bank

people: Inia Naiyaga (Deputy Governor, Reserve Bank of Fiji, retired May 2014; consultant to the SUN Insurance board from 2016; independent director April 2018; Managing Director from 6 June 2018)
summary: The Fiji Sun reports that SUN Insurance's board, through chairman Padam Raj Lala, appointed Inia Naiyaga as Managing Director effective 6 June, after chief executive Lolesh K. Sharma resigned. The same article states Naiyaga had been a consultant to the SUN board since 2016 and became an independent director in April 2018. On his public career it says he retired as Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of Fiji in May 2014, sat on the central bank's executive management team for 25 years, spent 40 years as a central banker, and served five years as Deputy Governor of the National Reserve Bank of Tonga. SUN Insurance is an insurance company, which this project counts as private finance; the article itself describes SUN only as a '100 per cent Fiji owned entity' and does not use the words private or state-owned.
source_title: Board Appoints Inia Naiyaga as SUN Insurance Managing Director (Fiji Sun, via PressReader)
move: central bank deputy governor to Managing Director of SUN Insurance

people: James H. Smith, CBE (Governor of the Central Bank of The Bahamas, 1987-1997; Chairman of CFAL, no dates given)
summary: CFAL, a Nassau financial firm, says on its own leadership page that James H. Smith is its Chairman and that he was Governor of the Central Bank of The Bahamas from 1987 to 1997. The page also lists public roles: Senator and Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance from 2002 to 2007, Undersecretary in the Cabinet Office, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Finance, Ambassador for Trade, and chairmanships of the Bahamas Maritime Authority, the Paradise Island Bridge Company and the Bahamas Development Bank, which is a government development bank. It says he has been a director on several private sector boards, without naming them, and gives no dates for the CFAL chairmanship. CFAL's own 'about' page describes the firm as 'a leading independent investment management and advisory firm based in Nassau, Bahamas', offering pension administration, brokerage and private wealth services, and says CFAL is 'the investment arm of Colina Holdings Ltd'. Neither page uses the words privately owned or government-owned, so the firm's ownership is stated only through that parent-company description. The private side of this career is CFAL; the Bahamas Development Bank and the ministry posts are the public side.
move: central bank governor to Chairman of CFAL, an investment management and brokerage firm

people: Sir Courtney Blackman (Economist, Irving Trust Company, 1968-1971; founding Governor of the Central Bank of Barbados, 1972-1987)
summary: The Central Bank of Barbados's own page for its past governors states that Sir Courtney Blackman worked from 1968 to 1971 as an economist at Irving Trust Company on Wall Street, which it calls 'now defunct', and that he was the founding Governor of the Central Bank of Barbados from 1972 to 1987, serving three terms, while also acting as Barbados' Alternate Governor to the IMF over the same period until March 1987. The same page says that from 1987 to 1994 he worked as an international business consultant to governments, central banks, multilateral institutions and international corporations, and served as Director General of several corporations and financial institutions, which it does not name. The page does not state whether Irving Trust Company or those later financial institutions were privately or publicly owned. The IMF alternate governorship is a public post.
source_title: Sir Courtney Blackman - Past Governors (Central Bank of Barbados)
move: Wall Street bank economist (Irving Trust Company) into the founding governorship; later unnamed financial-institution directorships after leaving

people: Sir Robin Fleming (former chief executive officer of Bank South Pacific; appointed to the Bank of Papua New Guinea board, announced April 2024) and Mark Baker (former ANZ country head; appointed to the same board)
summary: The PNG National Broadcasting Corporation reports that the Prime Minister announced new appointments to the Bank of Papua New Guinea board, in an article dated 10 April 2024 which says the announcement was made the previous day. It names Sir Robin Fleming as the 'former BSP chief executive officer', BSP being Bank South Pacific, and Mark Baker as the 'former ANZ Country Head', ANZ being Australia and New Zealand Banking. Both are commercial banks. The article also names Dairi Vele, a former Treasury Secretary, which is a government post, and Jeffery Yombon, a career Bank of PNG manager and assistant governor who became deputy governor. The article does not state whether Bank South Pacific or ANZ is privately or state-owned; ANZ is an Australian commercial bank and BSP is a commercial bank listed in Port Moresby, but that is not said in the source text. The Bank of PNG's own board page sets out only the board's legal composition and names no members or previous employers.
source_title: Former top bankers appointed to Central Bank Board (NBC PNG)
move: commercial bank chief executives (Bank South Pacific, ANZ) onto the central bank board

parties.party: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group

people: Dr Rama Krishna Sithanen (Chairperson and Director, International Financial Services, 2011-2016; Chairperson and Director, Sanne Mauritius, 2017-2022; Independent Chairperson and Director, Apex Group (Mauritius), 2023 to 15 November 2024; Governor of the Bank of Mauritius from 16 November 2024)
summary: The Bank of Mauritius publishes Sithanen's biodata on its own website. It states he became Governor with effect from 16 November 2024 for a three-year term, and that he was Independent Chairperson and Director of Apex Group (Mauritius) from 2023 until 15 November 2024, the day before he took office. Earlier it lists him as Chairperson and Director of Sanne Mauritius from 2017 to 2022 and of International Financial Services from 2011 to 2016, describing both as management companies providing fund administration and corporate services. Public-sector roles in the same document: Minister of Finance 1991-1995, Vice Prime Minister and Minister of Finance 2005-2010, Director of Strategy at the African Development Bank in 2011, Chairperson of the Rwanda Development Board 2013-2017, adviser to the Government of Rwanda 2013-2015, and Chairperson of Mauritius's Financial Services Commission from 11 December 2024. The three fund-administration companies are the private side; the biodata does not use the words private or state-owned for them, and it mentions no bank, insurer or brokerage. The African Development Bank role is a public move.
source_title: Governor Dr Rama Krishna Sithanen - Biodata (Bank of Mauritius)
move: chairman of Apex Group (Mauritius), a fund administration firm, directly into the governorship

people: Mohammed Said Mohammed Shahin (former Governor and Chairman of the Central Bank of Jordan and former Deputy Governor; Chairman of Islamic International Arab Bank since 31 March 2017)
summary: Islamic International Arab Bank states on its own board of directors page that its Chairman, Mohammed Said Mohammed Shahin, born 1948, joined the board on 31 March 2017, and that he is a former Chairman and Governor of the Central Bank of Jordan, a former Deputy Governor of the Central Bank, a former Chairman and Chief Executive of the Jordan Deposit Insurance Corporation, and a former director of several local and global corporations. No dates are given for those earlier posts. The Jordan Deposit Insurance Corporation is a state body, so that part of his career is public; the chairmanship of Islamic International Arab Bank, a commercial Islamic bank, is the private side. The same page shows that several other directors are serving executives of Arab Bank plc, including the vice chairman, who is Executive Vice President and Head of Consumer Banking at Arab Bank plc.
source_title: Board of Directors (Islamic International Arab Bank)
move: central bank governor to Chairman of Islamic International Arab Bank

people: Johannes !Gawaxab (appointed Governor of the Bank of Namibia, taking office 1 June 2020, succeeding Ipumbu Shiimi)
summary: Central Banking, in an article dated 22 April 2020, headlined 'Private sector banker appointed Bank of Namibia chief', reports that Johannes !Gawaxab was named by the Namibian president to lead the central bank and was set to take over from Ipumbu Shiimi on 1 June. The headline is the only place the article identifies him as coming from the private sector; the text names no firm, role or dates for any private financial employer, so this record carries the employer unnamed. The Bank of Namibia's own board page lists appointment dates for members but no previous employers at all, and no longer lists !Gawaxab, showing Ebson Uanguta as Governor from 1 January 2026.
source_title: Private sector banker appointed Bank of Namibia chief (Central Banking)
move: unnamed private-sector banking career into the governorship
